still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone; the GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived and Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.

The April 2033 Section 232 tariff of 100% on finished peptide drugs and peptide APIs from China and India is still in force, along with India's export-licence checks on direct-to-consumer incretin shipments.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 44.6% ever-used − 32.4% current = 12.2% of adults who used and are off now. About 55% of current users are on a second or later course (17.8 points), and 3.3 points cycled and are off again, so (17.8 + 3.3) / 44.6 ≈ 47.3% of ever-users have cycled. The other 8.9 points stopped once and have not restarted. One-year persistence is ~35–38% on cash oral products, ~60% in conditioned tracks and ~70% in military programmes, where command monitors fills. 40–48% restart within a year, and the falling TrumpRx maintenance prices pull restarters back. The 10.0-point rise in ever-use comes from oral amycretin at $299 on TrumpRx, accession waivers and military body-composition programmes, the VA/DoD AUD guideline and Medicaid AUD growth. Age check: 0.20×18.5 + 0.33×34.5 + 0.24×46.3 + 0.23×27 = 3.70 + 11.39 + 11.11 + 6.21 ≈ 32.4. Income thirds average 32.4. Users: 32.4% of ~276M adults ≈ 89.4M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial 20.0M (of which 11.8M are in conditioned tracks); Medicare 16.6M; Medicaid 5.6M (1.5M on the AUD label); TRICARE, VA and federal readiness programmes 1.5M; legitimate cash 40.5M (incl. ~8.5M who stay indefinitely on the $149 starting dose, ~2.9M on calm/focus plans and ~9.1M cash oral amycretin); imported or counterfeit 5.2M. Sum: 20.0 + 16.6 + 5.6 + 1.5 + 40.5 + 5.2 = 89.4. The bottom third rose 17.5 → 24.0 through the $149 starting dose, Medicaid AUD, military enlistees (who skew bottom- and middle-third) and EAP pill programmes at shift employers. About 21% of adults have obesity and are not on a drug. About half of them used one and stopped. They are concentrated in the rural South, among 65+ without qualifying codes, and among a new group: under-35s who are deliberately unmedicated, mostly upper-income. Adult obesity ~30.9%. Pediatric: 2.6% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 1.9M. That is ~4.8% of 12–17s and ~1.0% of 6–11s, up from 0.45% after the March 2036 Wegovy pill 6–11 approval and continued EPSDT weekly starts. About 62% of 6–11 users are on Medicaid/CHIP. About 6.4M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~16.6M users) still pays only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) and AUD codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 16.6M × ~$212 average net/month × 12 ≈ $42.2B gross Part D incretin spend (up from $38.3B). Users rose 19% while net price fell ~7%. Dementia route: ~2.6M × $225 × 12 ≈ $7.0B. AUD route: ~1.2M × $190 × 12 ≈ $2.7B. The CMS AUD coding audit (2034–35) recovered overpayments from three telehealth prescribers and left the code intact. Medicaid (~5.6M): AUD users rose 0.9M → 1.5M; ~1.5M × ~$110 net after rebates × 12 ≈ $2.0B. 6–11s are covered under EPSDT, and the same 7 states cover adult weight-loss use. TRICARE covers incretins for weight under DoD readiness policy. VA covers them only on existing codes, so separating service members lose weight-only coverage at discharge.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $3–25 a month in India and 100+ export markets. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials are $18–55 where patents are not enforced. Delivered to US addresses under the tariff, the same product costs ~$85–170. Canadian and Brazilian generics are CAD 40–70 and BRL 140–250. India and China still supply roughly two-thirds of world incretin volume. The WTO panel on the US tariff has been composed and has not ruled.
access.note: FICTIONAL. The decline was managed, and it happened in negotiated channels. Jan 2035 TrumpRx deal: oral amycretin $299, down from ~$449 cash direct. Wegovy pill maintenance $179, down from $199, with the starting dose still $149. Foundayo $149–199. Injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $199–249. MariTide $219 direct. Retatrutide ~$349 cash, the only brand above $300 outside list price. DLA buys for DoD at a contract price of ~$110/month. Business Group on Health (Nov 2036): 34% of employers cover weight-management use, roughly unchanged. About two-thirds condition it on adherence and ≥5% progress, and ~40% of those now allow 'logged holidays' of up to 14 days a quarter without losing the tier. Conditioned tracks hold 11.8M of the 20.0M commercial users. Orals are ~66% of users, and oral amycretin has ~13.5M users across payers. The gray market shrank slightly to 5.2M. Domestic re-filling from smuggled API persists in the Gulf South, and counterfeit serialised pens now sell mainly as cheap amycretin.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral (oral amycretin)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody muscle adjunct (bimagrumab, restricted label)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide / Wegovy pill). The VA/DoD clinical practice guideline (Jun 2035) lists it as a first-line option alongside naltrexone and acamprosate

pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide since Feb 2034; daily Wegovy pill since Mar 2036, all with 6-monthly growth-velocity, Tanner staging and eating-disorder screening language)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: deliberate 'drug holidays', meaning skipped weekends or off-weeks, especially on short-half-life Foundayo
calm/focus low-dose plans via telehealth (~2.9M subscribers, high churn)
dementia-prevention use by 60+ without CVD, cash-paid, while the tirzepatide extension is under review
indefinite use of the $149 TrumpRx starting dose (~8.5M people)
unit-level 'readiness' use by police and fire officers beyond grant eligibility criteria
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral-parity driver is honoured by the existing product. Oral amycretin (approved Feb 2034, ~21.5%) reached a $299 TrumpRx price in Jan 2035, was approved by EMA in Jun 2035, and pushed orals to ~66% of US users. No oral matches retatrutide's ~24%, and none is under review. The pediatric under-12 driver is realised by a new form of an existing product. The Wegovy pill sNDA for ages 6–11 (filed Jan 2035) was approved Mar 2036, 14 months later, with the weekly product's monitoring language and a medication guide, and no REMS. The AUD driver is realised through guidelines. The VA/DoD CPG (Jun 2035) makes the Wegovy pill first-line, and no new AUD molecule was filed. Lilly resubmitted the tirzepatide dementia 60+ without CVD extension in Apr 2035. FDA extended the PDUFA date to Jan 2037 to review hip-fracture data in women 70+, and the extension is not approved. Implants remain in phase 2 and are not on the market. Global incretin market ~$225B (2035). US branded net prices drift down ~4% a year.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Drug holidays on weekly and long-half-life products produce re-titration nausea when users restart at full dose, a common ED presentation on Mondays.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. Labels already advise re-titration after missed doses, and clinicians now counsel it actively.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The first two MDL bellwethers (2035) split. One was a defence verdict, and the other awarded a cycler $11M against Novo, which is on appeal. Claims are ~43,000. Cohort data on persistence after stopping are still disputed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling. More bellwethers are set for 2037.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low; still pleaded with EPI.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after >2 years and ~1.45 after ≥3 cycles, unchanged. Army body-composition data show lean-mass loss is blunted in units with mandatory strength programming.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained. The hip-fracture excess is why FDA extended the PDUFA date on the tirzepatide dementia extension. Bimagrumab is still restricted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low. FAA aeromedical guidance requires an eye-exam attestation for pilots.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No signal in adults, including AUD-label and military users.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 2033 FDA observational estimate still stands: ~7% vs ~3.5% at maintenance doses, ~10% on retatrutide. An NIH-funded low-dose study is enrolling and has not reported. No new data changed the picture. The complaint is now general and self-managed through holidays and dose step-downs.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. FDA stays at 'hypothesis-generating'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after cycles. Partial regain during repeated holidays is now measurable in track data. Separating service members who lose TRICARE coverage are a new regain cohort.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins conditioned coverage and logged-holiday caps.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D and thiamine (in AUD users who keep drinking) deficiencies continue. Low ferritin in adolescent girls continues.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language and thiamine counselling retained.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Still ~2× incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. EPI claims are ~61,000. The DOJ civil investigative demand is unresolved, and Novo's reserve is unchanged at $6.2B.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled for both. The FDA Form 483 was closed out after corrective action (2035).

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. Cycling and holiday patterns are poorly characterised. There are still no data on indefinite starting-dose use or on daily oral exposure from age 6.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth PMRs continue and were extended to the Wegovy pill 6–11.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~36,000. Re-filling operations persist in Mississippi, Alabama and Louisiana. A second, smaller CDC infection cluster (~70 cases, 1 death, 2035) appeared. Poison-centre calls are flat at ~5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Tariff and export checks unchanged; no statute or state action.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Prepubertal height velocity on liraglutide and semaglutide is still ~0.5–0.6 cm/year below expected, with partial catch-up after stopping. The Wegovy pill 6–11 trial showed a similar ~0.5 cm/year deficit. Swedish ARFID HR ~1.8. Final adult height is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Monitoring language and medication guide, no REMS. AAP still prefers lifestyle-first for prepubertal children.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ED network rate ~1 per 2,400 person-years. Cases are concentrated in titration and in restarts after holidays. Military ASAP clinics report few cases under supervised titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label counselling retained. The postmarketing study's interim report found no new signal.

food_and_beverage.state: About half of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~16% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~14%. The 2033 'tariff bounce' faded as priced-out users moved to the $149 pill. Dollar sales are down ~2% in two years. Large packaged-food firms sell smaller packs and protein lines. A small premium counter-trend is growing: whole-grain bread, butter and long-ferment bakery tied to the Whole Appetite movement is double-digit growth in Asheville, Portland and the Hudson Valley, but it is a rounding error nationally.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~21% from 2025 and beer ~14%. The VA/DoD guideline put the AUD pill into base ASAP clinics. Navy and Army club and exchange alcohol sales fell ~18%. Bardstown bourbon makers cut a further ~900 jobs, and two mid-sized distilleries sold aged stock to private-label exporters. Non-alcoholic drinks are ~6% of category dollars.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. Portion tiers and smaller plates are standard in casual dining. Bar revenue stays depressed in Dayton, Toledo and around bases near Fayetteville and Killeen. A visible niche of 'long table' prix-fixe restaurants markets abundance to unmedicated diners, and some ban phones and pill timers at the table.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Mass retailers run size-flex lines for cyclers and holiday-takers. Whole Appetite has an aesthetic of loose undyed linen, high waists, bare unbanded wrists and visible softness, and small labels and Etsy-scale makers sell it. Structured athletic wear keeps growing.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing on track InBody requirements and mandatory strength programming in military body-composition programmes. Police departments on readiness grants contract budget gyms. Family strength programmes are steady.

insurance.state: Structure unchanged: 34% of employers cover, two-thirds of them with conditions. New this step: 'logged holiday' clauses capped at 14 days a quarter, which vendors verify from pill-bottle logs. Pharmacy trend is ~+6%, with price declines partly offsetting volume. Part D premiums rose again for 2036.

pharma.state: Growing on volume while net price falls. Novo's oral amycretin is the class's biggest product by US users, while litigation and the DOJ inquiry continue. Lilly holds the injectable tier and Foundayo. DLA's DoD contract (~$110/month) became a reference point in PBM negotiations. Amgen's MariTide grows inside tracks. Indian exporters' US direct-to-consumer volume has not recovered.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body reads as who pays and how strictly they watch. A lean recruit at Fort Jackson is a waiver. A soft, unbanded wrist in Asheville is a declaration. Monday-heavy and Friday-light is a Foundayo holiday-taker. A slow regain after leaving the Army is the gap between TRICARE and the VA.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle and 'off-drug lean' remain the upper-tier boast. Among college-educated women aged 22–34, a visible unmedicated body has become a status claim of its own, legible as 'I can afford not to'. The drug spreads fastest now through the bottom and middle thirds, via $149 pills, Medicaid AUD and enlistment waivers. Medicaid children are still most 6–11 starts, now increasingly on a daily tablet.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals stay shorter in medicated households. Whole Appetite holds 'long tables', public Sunday suppers in Asheville that draw several hundred people, with bread broken by hand and no pill timers. Bread Alone congregations, now ~1,300, co-host many of them. Military dining facilities in Fort Bragg and Fort Hood serve smaller default portions and a protein line.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added 'unmedicated' as a tag beside 'calm plan' and 'on AUD treatment'. It is the fastest-growing tag among under-30s in college towns. Couples plan holiday weekends together: off the Foundayo Friday to Sunday so that food, wine and desire come back, then back on Monday.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is now a thing people negotiate on a schedule as well as manage. The complaint 'I can't feel anything' is ordinary small talk. Whole Appetite turns appetite into an identity and a politics: eat, want, refuse the log. It draws MAHA parents, Unmuted chapters and secular young women in one loose coalition, with fat-acceptance groups still separate and wary.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Measured blunting is unchanged (~7% vs ~3.5% at maintenance doses; ~10% on retatrutide; low doses unmeasured). What changed is the talk about it. A national poll (Nov 2035, KFF-style) found 41% of current users say the drug 'dulls things I care about' at least sometimes, and ~35% of maintenance users report deliberate holidays in the past six months. Holidays work pharmacologically on Foundayo (half-life ~1–2 days). They do little on weekly semaglutide or oral semaglutide (~1 week), and clinicians say so. Calm-plan subscriptions grew only 2.4M → 2.9M, with ~45% annual churn.
interior_life.framing: Mostly a side effect people manage themselves: 'the flatness', solved with 'Fridays off'. Platforms quietly dropped 'quiet the noise' for 'find your dose'. Manufacturers still say 'food noise'. The military says 'readiness'. Whole Appetite calls the drug 'the leash'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: 11.8M employees are in conditioned tracks, and logged-holiday caps now turn mood management into a benefits event. Under the DoD readiness directive, service members in body-composition programmes cannot take holidays without command approval, and missed fills appear on unit readiness dashboards. FAA guidance requires pilots to be stable on a dose for 3 months, with no holidays during flight duty. COPS-funded police programmes in ~430 departments log adherence. The two EEOC charges remain unresolved.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Flat' became a music-critic adjective, and there is a minor genre of 'Friday records' made on holiday weekends. Whole Appetite publishes cookbooks and zines. Its Asheville 'Long Table' festival is a small pilgrimage. Bar-dependent live-music venues in Columbus and Louisville keep shrinking, and daytime and all-ages shows grow.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Holiday weekends structure sex and appetite for many couples. Therapists report mismatched schedules, one partner on Foundayo holidays and the other on a weekly shot that can't be paused. Couples where one partner is unmedicated by conviction describe it as a values difference rather than a medical one.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The complaint is bipartisan small talk. Whole Appetite has a pledge, the 'Own Appetite' pledge, that ~140 local and state candidates signed for 2036, promising to oppose conditioned premiums and pediatric starts. No state passed anything. Veterans' groups lobby on the TRICARE-to-VA coverage gap. 'Sedated electorate' claims still have no turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal, routine and permissive on approvals: the Wegovy pill for 6–11 in 2036, and a PDUFA extension for the dementia extension rather than a rejection. Punitive on imports, with the tariff unchanged. No state legislature or agency acted, and Illinois's ban is still the only one.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No change in who pays civilians. The new money is federal workforce money. DoD's Metabolic Readiness directive (Mar 2035) funds TRICARE and direct-care incretins for body-composition and accession programmes. FICTIONAL arithmetic: ~125k active-duty users × ~$110 DLA price × 12 ≈ $165M/year. DOJ COPS 'Officer Readiness' grants total $190M over FY2035–36, covering ~43k officers in ~430 departments: 43k × ~$185 × 12 ≈ $95M/year. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Deeper again. Adherence feeds now reach unit readiness dashboards in the military, and police wellness vendors in grant departments receive them too. Employer tracks verify logged holidays from smart-bottle data. FEHB carriers receive adherence feeds, and two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage.
state.workforce_or_military: The DoD directive expanded the Army recruit oral pilot to all services. Applicants up to 6 points over body-fat standards can enlist on a supervised oral incretin, ~19k accessions a year. The Army Body Composition Program adds the drug alongside mandatory strength programming. The VA/DoD guideline puts the AUD pill first-line in base substance-use clinics. FAA aeromedical guidance formalised incretin use for pilots after 3 months stable. FMCSA still covers on-label AUD use by drivers and is still silent on calm plans and holidays. Separating service members keep TRICARE coverage only for transitional periods, and the VA covers only existing codes.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The 100% Section 232 tariff and the Indian export checks stand. The WTO panel on China's complaint has been composed and has not ruled. DoD's supply contract requires US- or Danish-made product and cites 'readiness supply security'. Indian exporters' volume moved to the Gulf, Latin America and Africa. Smuggled API still feeds domestic re-filling.

events.event: TrumpRx adds oral amycretin at $299 a month, down from about $449, and cuts Wegovy pill maintenance to $179 and injectable Wegovy and Zepbound to $199–249; the $149 starting dose is unchanged

Pentagon issues a Metabolic Readiness directive: all services may enlist applicants over body-fat limits on supervised oral incretins, body-composition programmes add the drug, and DLA signs a ~$110-a-month supply contract; DOJ opens $190M in COPS 'Officer Readiness' grants and FAA formalises pilot guidance

VA and DoD update their alcohol use disorder guideline to list the Wegovy pill as a first-line option alongside naltrexone; base substance-use clinics begin prescribing it, and exchange alcohol sales fall

A national poll finds 41% of incretin users say the drug dulls things they care about and a third take deliberate 'drug holidays'; within months ~40% of conditioned employer tracks add 'logged holiday' allowances of up to 14 days a quarter

FDA approves the daily Wegovy pill for children 6–11, with the same growth-monitoring language as the weekly shot and no REMS; Medicaid prescribers say most new pediatric starts are switching to the tablet

Whole Appetite's 'Long Table' weekend in Asheville draws about 25,000 people; organisers unveil an 'Own Appetite' pledge against conditioned premiums and pediatric starts, signed by ~140 candidates by autumn

open_tensions: Holidays against logs. A third of users manage blunting by skipping doses, which works on Foundayo and barely works on semaglutide. Meanwhile employer tracks cap holidays, and the military forbids them without command approval. Restart nausea and partial regain are the price, and nobody has studied the pattern.

A daily tablet from age 6. Children starting it are still mostly on Medicaid, growth deficits of ~0.5 cm a year are replicated across three products, final adult height is unknown, and the unmedicated movement has made those children its cause.

Readiness without an exit. About 19k people a year now enlist on the drug, and police departments log officers' adherence. But the VA does not cover weight-only use, so the drug that got people into uniform ends at discharge, and a regain cohort of veterans is forming.

Cheaper pills and the tariff. Managed decline pulled the bottom third in at $149–299, yet 5.2M people still buy imported or re-filled product. Smuggled API still kills people in the Gulf South, and the WTO panel has not ruled.

prose.headline: One in Three, Weekends Off: The Pill Enlists, Kids Get a Tablet, and the Unmedicated Set the Long Table
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 about a third of American adults take an incretin drug, close to ninety million people, and nearly half have tried one. Most of them swallow it. Two-thirds of users are on a daily pill. The pill that made the difference, Novo's oral amycretin, matches the injectables' weight loss and since January 2035 has cost $299 a month through TrumpRx. Prices fell the way Washington likes them to fall, by deal rather than collapse. The Wegovy maintenance pill is $179, and the shots are around $200 to $250. The $149 starting dose is unchanged, and eight and a half million people still live on it indefinitely. The list price is still $1,349, and no generic is coming. Medicare still pays nothing for weight alone.

Who pays did not change. A third of employers cover the drugs, and two-thirds of those still require a log, a scan and five percent off in six months. What changed is what people say about it. In November 2035 a national poll found that four in ten users say the drug dulls things they care about. A third take what everyone now calls drug holidays: Friday to Sunday off, a week off before a wedding. Pharmacists explain that a holiday works on Lilly's short-acting Foundayo and barely registers on semaglutide, which stays in the body for a week, but people do it anyway. Employers adapted. Many tracks now allow fourteen logged holiday days a quarter, verified by the smart bottle. Calm-plan platforms stopped promising quiet and started selling help finding your dose.

The federal government found a new reason to want people on the drug: readiness. In March 2035 the Pentagon let every service enlist applicants over the body-fat limit if they take a supervised pill. About nineteen thousand recruits a year now come in that way. Body-composition programmes pair the drug with mandatory lifting, the Defense Logistics Agency buys it for about $110 a month, and missed fills show up on unit dashboards. The VA and DoD named the alcohol pill a first-line treatment, and sales at base clubs fell. The Justice Department funded drug programmes in some four hundred police departments. The FAA wrote down how pilots may fly on it. When a soldier leaves the service, though, the coverage stops, because the VA pays only for diabetes and the other old codes.

The children's question did not go away; it changed form. In March 2036 the FDA approved the daily Wegovy pill for six-to-eleven-year-olds, with the same instruction to measure height every six months. Its trial showed the same half-centimetre-a-year slowing as the weekly shot. Most young users are on Medicaid, and their prescribers are moving them to the tablet.

The new thing is a movement of people who choose not to take it. Whole Appetite began in Asheville among college-educated women in their twenties and early thirties, joined by Bread Alone congregations and the remnants of Unmuted. Its look is undyed linen, a bare wrist and a visible belly, and it holds long Sunday tables where bread is torn by hand and no one sets a pill timer. In May its Long Table weekend drew twenty-five thousand people, and by autumn about 140 candidates had signed its pledge against conditioned premiums and pediatric starts. Its critics note that refusing a drug is easiest for people who can afford the gym. No state passed anything.

The ledger holds. No new safety signal appeared. Pancreatic-insufficiency claims passed sixty thousand, and the first stomach-paralysis trials split. The tariff still stands, and back-room vials in Mississippi still make people sick. Spirits volumes are down a fifth from 2025, and snack volumes are down a sixth. The country is calmer and leaner, increasingly in uniform, and it takes weekends off when its benefits plan allows.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Officer Renée Kowalczyk wakes at 5:10 in Dayton, and the bottle on the nightstand blinks green. It is Thursday, so she takes the pill. The department's Officer Readiness grant pays for the Foundayo, and the wellness vendor gets the cap's timestamp before she has brushed her teeth. She has used nine holiday days this quarter. That leaves five, which is enough for her sister's wedding in Toledo and nothing more.

Roll call. Sergeant Diaz reads the stolen-catalytic-converter list. Somebody's protein shake sweats on the table, and nobody eats the donuts.

At noon she sits in the cruiser outside a closed bar on Wayne Avenue, which has a FOR LEASE sign and a chalkboard still offering PILL NIGHT, MOCKTAILS $6. She eats half a turkey wrap and puts the other half back in the foil without thinking about it.

At 4:30 her daughter Maya, seventeen, is in the kitchen kneading something, flour up to the elbows. She wears a linen shirt and has no watch. A Whole Appetite flyer is held to the fridge by a magnet: LONG TABLE, SUNDAY, ST. ANNE'S HALL.

"You should come," Maya says.

"I'm on Sunday."

"You're always on."

Renée watches the dough rise and fall under her daughter's hands. She remembers wanting bread like that, with butter, the whole heel.

At nine her husband pours himself a beer and offers her the bottle out of habit. She shakes her head and isn't sure whether she's saying no to the beer or to something else.

In bed she opens the vendor app and taps HOLIDAY: SAT–SUN. It asks for a reason, and she types: wedding. Four days left.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pharmacists explain that a holiday works on Lilly's short-acting Foundayo and barely registers on semaglutide, which stays in the body for a week
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the claim that a third of users take drug holidays rests on a pharmacology that the same text says does not work for most users, since oral semaglutide and weekly shots are the bulk of volume. The holiday behaviour is asserted as widespread with no shown chain explaining why people persist.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Applicants up to 6 points over body-fat standards can enlist on a supervised oral incretin, ~19k accessions a year.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: ~19k accessions plus ~125k active-duty users are asked to explain a large part of the 10.0-point rise in ever-use (about 27M adults) and the bottom third's jump from 17.5 to 24. Military and police programmes (~1.5M TRICARE/VA/federal users) cannot carry that much of the change.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Whole Appetite's 'Long Table' weekend in Asheville draws about 25,000 people; organisers unveil an 'Own Appetite' pledge against conditioned premiums and pediatric starts, signed by ~140 candidates by autumn
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a new movement goes from nothing to 25,000 attendees and 140 candidate signatories in about two years. The causal chain is thin, and the movement is fully formed, branded and aesthetically coded with no seed in the 2034 world.

rationale.badness: Measured against 2026, this world keeps the inherited harms (a ~54k-to-61k-claim EPI mass tort, hip-fracture HR 1.3–1.45, pediatric growth deficits now on a daily tablet from age 6, a persistent gray market with Burkholderia clusters) and adds deeper conditioning. Premium tiers hinge on pill-bottle logs, and military readiness dashboards track missed fills, with holidays barred without command approval. Autonomy and inequality are the heaviest dimensions, since coverage is conditioned, veterans lose weight-only coverage at discharge, and the bottom third is only partly reached. It is a recognisably harder society, but the harm is measured and discussed, and the 41% complaint is openly aired, so epistemic and cohesion stay mid-range.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visible. Managed decline appears as TrumpRx cuts, status quo on coverage holds at 34% of employers, the pediatric under-12 driver comes as the Wegovy pill 6–11, AUD arrives via the VA/DoD guideline, oral parity, the military workforce driver, mainstream_complaint and natural_movement all appear, and no safety signal or market shock is added. mechanism: Several shifts are asserted. The holiday phenomenon contradicts the pharmacology the text itself gives (claim 1), and Whole Appetite appears fully formed (claim 3). The pill 6–11 approval 14 months after a Jan 2035 filing is permitted. magnitude: Headline figures sit inside the envelope (32.4% on drug, 44.6% ever, which is under 45.3), and the payer mix sums to 89.4M. The 10-point ever-use rise leans on tiny military and police populations (claim 2) and on oral amycretin. The Medicare spend of 16.6M × $212 × 12 ≈ $42.2B checks out, but the dementia route (~2.6M, obesity plus CVD) and AUD route (~1.2M) sit awkwardly with the stated user counts and the small AUD population, so reconciliation is only partly clean.
rationale.generativity: The prose carries a specific officer, a blinking bottle, a holiday-day count, a closed bar with a leftover PILL NIGHT sign, and a daughter kneading bread with a flyer on the fridge. These imply many scenes. The world fields supply rich texture such as Monday ED nausea, 'Friday records' and wrist-bare fashion, though the day-in-the-life ends somewhat tidily on the quota gag.

least_plausible_claims.quote: a national poll finds 41% of incretin users say the drug dulls things they care about and a third take deliberate 'drug holidays'; within months ~40% of conditioned employer tracks add 'logged holiday' allowances
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: employer tracks that conditioned coverage on adherence loosen within months of a poll. Only a pharmacology-based rationale is given, with no benefit-design or cost-driven chain. It also sits oddly with 'about 35% of maintenance users report deliberate holidays' when the flat FDA rate is ~7%.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Applicants up to 6 points over body-fat standards can enlist on a supervised oral incretin, ~19k accessions a year.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: ~125k active-duty users on drug and 19k accessions a year as a result of a directive from one year earlier is a very fast ramp. The ~1.5M TRICARE/VA/readiness payer bucket also looks large relative to the stated DoD and COPS programme spending, which implies only ~125k + 43k users.

rationale.badness: Compared with 2026, the world has about a third of adults on drug, with adherence-conditioned coverage for 11.8M people, adherence feeds reaching military unit dashboards and police vendors, and daily pills for 6–11-year-olds with a growth deficit of ~0.5 cm/yr. Added to this are 61,000 EPI claims, hip-fracture HR ~1.3–1.45, a re-filled-vial cluster in the Gulf South, a veteran regain cohort, and a 41% 'dulls things' complaint. Mitigations are access broadening to the bottom third and the fact that the harms are named and discussed (a poll, the FDA study, MDL trials), so the epistemic score is moderate. Surveillance and conditioning are normalised, which keeps autonomy high.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All drivers are visibly realised. Managed decline comes through the TrumpRx cuts, status-quo coverage holds at 34%, and pediatric under-12 comes through the Wegovy pill 6–11 as a new form of an existing product. AUD comes through the VA/DoD guideline, oral parity through oral amycretin, workforce_military through the DoD directive, mainstream_complaint through the poll, and natural_movement through Whole Appetite; none is contradicted. mechanism: The military and pediatric chains are shown. The Whole Appetite scale and the fast employer holiday clauses are asserted (claims 1 and 2). The unmedicated group being mostly upper-income is plausibly derived. magnitude: Adults on drug 32.4 and ever-used 44.6 are inside the envelope (30.4–34.4; 34.6–45.3), and the income thirds bracket the national figure. However, the $42.2B total is not consistent with its own parts, the 1.5M military/readiness bucket is large against the programme spending (claim 3), and the fast ramp of the military pill is questionable.
rationale.generativity: The Dayton officer vignette shows rather than explains: the bottle blinking green, the vendor timestamp, the holiday-day budget, the PILL NIGHT sign, her daughter kneading bread and the Whole Appetite flyer, and the beer she isn't sure she is refusing. Strong secondary characters and scenes are implied (Sergeant Diaz, Maya, a Long Table Sunday). The prose summary is more explanatory, but the world offers a lot of film.
